Companion guides (this site)

  • Wire up Deploy App TAK Servers via a Federation Hub (IaC) — the prerequisite: each hub and its servers, brought up by IaC. This guide adds only the hub-to-hub link on top.
  • Federation Hub — concepts: hub-and-spoke, multi-hop, the policy graph (CA Group, Outgoing, Token Group nodes), edges, and group filtering. The Outgoing-to-another-hub capability is what makes hub-to-hub work.
  • Integrating to TAK Server — the Marti API and group model used by the cross-domain verification probes.

Official guides

  • Federation Hub Configuration Guide (public release) — multi-hop hub-to-hub, ports (9100/9102/9103), federation-hub-broker.yml and federation-hub-ui.yml, the policy (CA Group, Outgoing, Token Group; edges; Allow All / Allowed / Disallowed filtering), token auth, and MFDT.
  • TAK Server Configuration Guide — §12 Federation and federated group mapping (the per-link group filtering the hub edges build on).

Key facts used here

  • A Federation Hub Outgoing node can target another Federation Hub (multi-hop) on the peer's v2 port 9102.
  • Hub-to-hub is mutual TLS: cross-trust each hub's CA into the other's fed-truststore.jks; one side initiates.
  • The inter-hub edge is filtered (Allowed Groups = SHARED_COP); data is filtered at each hop, and both hubs must allow the shared group.
  • The shared group name must be identical across all deployments in both domains (one shared Keycloak tak_<group> taxonomy).
  • Token auth (9103) is the fallback for links that cannot pass mTLS.
  • Enable MFDT (MongoDB) for store-and-forward across disrupted inter-hub links.

Status and scope

Draft / proposed design, not yet demoed. Built from Deploy App's docker-rasenmaeher-integration templates and the public TAK Server and Federation Hub configuration guides. The single open item, the policy artifact and apply mechanism for your FedHub version, is the same one noted in the single-hub guide. Civilian; no TAK-MIL content.
